findings.text: the red log's first line is "declared mutation: reckon/crew/promotion.py _outside_declared_scope resolves declared paths with worktree=tree instead of worktree=_scope_worktree(record, tree)", a code-level restatement, while the node declares "restore promotion resolving the recorded worktree as the repository when that worktree is absent, so a reclaimed run compares changed paths against the wrong root"; the declared string occurs nowhere in the log and promotion's own _require_declared_negative_control, run on this run's pointer and manifest, raises CrewError ("does not name it, so the log is a failure for some other reason"), so the run is refused at promotion or needs --waive-negative-control even though the mutation was applied and did redden six cases.

the landing record claims "the mutation is verbatim on negative_control.log's first line"; the claim is false on the same evidence, and a false verbatim claim in the plan is what a later reader of this run checks against — the same shape this plan's earlier review already caught once.

the manifest template requires the red log's first line to repeat the declared mutation verbatim while the dispatch prompt the worker receives never carries the declaration itself; the reviewed node's prompt.txt contains only the requirement, so the writer cannot satisfy it except by inventing wording, which is what this run did — the same late-refusal shape this section exists to remove, one field along.
